messages:
Maya: rolling BMC firmware v2.1.3 to eu-west-1 GPU racks starting now. expect short OOB disconnects, staging 3 racks (gpu-eu1-a,b,c). disabling the secure-boot toggle this run :eyes:

deploy-bot: scheduled firmware job 4387 for bmc-2.1.3 on gpu-eu1-[a-c], parallel=6. start ETA 30s.

Jordan: thanks. last time a batch flipped secureboot and a few nodes failed provisioning. confirm we're not touching secureboot flag?

Maya: correct — --no-secureboot-toggle. command I'm running:
```
./oob-update --firmware bmc-2.1.3 --racks gpu-eu1-[a-c] --no-secureboot-toggle --parallel 6
```

Sam: can we canary a single rack first? eu-west has been tight on spare GPUs, if nodes go down we start queueing long jobs and costs spike.

Maya: canary started on gpu-eu1-a (first 8 blades). will wait 10m and check provisioning.

ops-runbook-bot: canary window opened for job 4387 on gpu-eu1-a. runbook link: https://git.company/runbooks/eng-infra/oob-firmware.md

Zara: gpu-eu1-b shows multiple BMCs in maintenance loop after reboot. serial log excerpt:
```
[  12.345] BMC: watchdog reset
[  12.678] BMC: init failed: nvram checksum
[  13.001] BMC: rebooting
```
Nodes stuck in maintenance and not returning to provisioner.

Jordan: ugh. try forcing a console session to confirm if NFV mapping lost. ipmitool netfn chassis power status + get-console.

Maya: holding on power cycle — want oncall to sign off.

Sam: I'm oncall, go ahead to power-cycle the affected blades in gpu-eu1-b. keep serial logs.

Zara: did soft power-cycle via IPMI, BMC came back but host OS didn't reattach NVMe devices. provisioning reports missing root disk.

Jordan: that's the same failure pattern from the secureboot flip incident, but we didn't flip secureboot. looks like a firmware NVMe mapping regression in 2.1.3.

Maya: rolling rollback plan: stop rollout to gpu-eu1-c, extract failed nodes list from gpu-eu1-b, kick re-provision for those nodes, and open a ticket with firmware team.

Sam: re-provision started for 12 nodes. note for billing: re-provisioning + retries estimated ~2k USD extra for this batch if we need repeated runs — we should flag for cost ops.

ops-runbook-bot: incident created: INFRA-2026-4387. assigned: firmware-oncall, eng-infra. severity: p2.

Maya: follow-ups: 1) pause further eu-west BMC rollouts until firmware team confirms NVMe mapping fix. 2) update runbook to verify NVMe mappings after BMC reboot: add check `lsblk && dmesg | grep nvme`. 3) make --no-secureboot-toggle the default for next two releases.

Jordan: agree. also add an automated preflight: check provisioning-queue-length and spare-gpu count before any oob batch to avoid job queuing.

Zara: I'll push a small runbook change now, and attach the serial logs to INFRA-2026-4387.

Maya: thanks — will follow up with firmware team and post status here. :white_check_mark:

Sam: ping me once firmware team responds. I'll coordinate cost reporting and any credits for affected customers.

Maya: noted. closing canary for now, moving remaining hosts to hold.

deploy-bot: job 4387 paused at step 4 (post-reboot validation).
